hints: Write the SI base units for the three quantities: $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$, $\Delta P$ in $\text{Pa}$ or $\text{kg m}^{-1} \text{s}^{-2}$, and $\rho$ in $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
First simplify the units inside the bracket $\Delta P/\rho$ by cancelling $\text{kg}$ and combining powers of $\text{m}$.
Compare the power of $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$ from $(\text{m}^2 \text{s}^{-2})^n$ with $\text{m}^1 \text{s}^{-1}$ to find $n$, remembering $k$ has no units.
walkthrough: The equation must be homogeneous, so both sides must have the units of speed, $\text{m s}^{-1}$, and $k$ can be ignored because it has no units.
Write $\Delta P$ in base units: pressure = force/area, so $1 \text{ Pa} = 1 \text{ N m}^{-2} = 1 \text{ kg m}^{-1} \text{s}^{-2}$.
Write density in base units: $\rho$ has units $\text{kg m}^{-3}$. Hence $\frac{\Delta P}{\rho}$ has units $\frac{\text{kg m}^{-1} \text{s}^{-2}}{\text{kg m}^{-3}} = \text{m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$.
Raise this to power $n$: the right-hand side has units $(\text{m}^2 \text{s}^{-2})^n = \text{m}^{2n} \text{s}^{-2n}$.

A.explanation: The base units of $\Delta P/\rho$ are $\text{m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$, so power $n=1/2$ gives $\text{m s}^{-1}$ for $v$.

B.explanation: With $n=1$, the right-hand side has units $\text{m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$, which is not a speed.

C.explanation: With $n=3/2$, the right-hand side has units $\text{m}^3 \text{s}^{-3}$, which is not a speed.

D.explanation: With $n=2$, the right-hand side has units $\text{m}^4 \text{s}^{-4}$, which is not a speed.
